item.title: Draft "Disconnected Restroom": Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Followup response to PM:

I personally didn't find the draft that interesting—it seemed like the majority of the description was about the non-anomalous features. The actual anomaly itself wasn't clear until I reread the entirety of the description. The logs were pretty bland and generic horror material, especially the last log that had an incident that seemed gratuitous/shoehorned just to artificially introduce previously unmentioned danger.

Would you like a full review of the draft (there were a lot of small clinical tone errors, and spots where I felt the text could be slimmed down) or would you like me to discuss the concept first?

item.title: Screams: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Damien Loth, instead of replying to your own comments, please edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of every comment. That prevents spam buildup, and it's in the rules.

Also, most reviewers prefer to review sandbox drafts. Keeping your draft in a Google doc not only makes it more difficult to check if your wikidot coding works, it also can be a security risk for private information (IRL name, email addresses, etc.) that may be inadvertently revealed when sharing via the Google suite.

item.title: Draft "Disconnected Restroom": Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
I gave your draft a read through. Please note, I'm not a critter and will be providing feedback as a reader / author.

Crit
Hide

Your formatting of the ConProcs is visually distracting. The hallway is located within Provisional Site-XXXX, so you should establish the existence of the site first instead of at the end. The post-incident adjustments can be incorporated into the normal ConProcs; having it as an add-on doesn't benefit the story or anything.

Your description should state what the SCP is first, then where it is located. The description still has general grammar errors and a lot of text that comes off as non-clinical.

I lost interest after the description because there just really isn't anything interesting there. In a 340 word description, all you've really told me is that it's two washrooms (one for men, one for women) not connected to utilities but still working inside an office building.

If the "meat" comes later, it's important to ensure the reader doesn't become uninterested before then.

item.title: A wholesome tale in these trying times: Re: A wholesome tale in these trying times
item.content:encoded:
Auww, that was a really adorable story, I thoroughly enjoyed that, Raddagher!

I tried my best to put on my scrutiny glasses along the way, to see if I could spot any flaws, but I didn't see any and eventually got distracted by the story to the point that I sort of forgot to pay attention to those, which is a compliment I guess.

The pacing was really good, the paragraphs are broken up in a way as to make reading easy, and the writing was effortless to follow.

item.title: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone: Re: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I like the idea of presenting this as like… vast sea creature that feeds off humans and lives in the depths and like…as if it's something to be scared of before the ending reveals they're actually looking for love; but something about the way this is done feels…iffy?

I think it's because the SCP just, immediately tells us with no real build up or anything; it's just, passive story being told and then ending 'oh yeah i feel in love' and it feels like it needs…more showing? Like, there's a version of this I can see where you completely strip out the interview logs and add a short addendum that implies a few details that in turn imply the love angle where it feels like this might hit harder; or alternatively taking the love angle and actually running with it, exploring the kinda…sadness of the angler fish as they make someone they love part of themselves but in turn, slowly lose everything about the person that they fell in love with, y'know? Really play with this in a deeply emotional way.

Part of me wonders if the description could be trimmed down a lot: like, there's some big paragraphs about the mating behaviour of these things and I wonder whether there's a better way of conveying them than dense prose; perhaps just leaving it somewhat implied and only covering it in very broad strokes? Same goes for a lot of the details about -1: I wonder whether there's a way to nail the emotions here without spending so much time setting everything up exactly?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Coastal regions most frequented by SCP-X are to monitored weekly by local marine vessels equipped with sonar capable of bathymetric mapping.

the 'most frequented' here feels clunky; perhaps just cutting the most would help? It might be that 'SCP-X' is read as a singular thing and so adding 'instances' after to emphasise that there's a whole bunch of them would help?

SCP-X-1 and any other captured instances are to held at Site-66 in a saltwater tank set to mimic ocean

I'd slap commas are 'and any other capture instances' so this flows better

The tank is to undergo monthly cleaning and upkeep and is to coincide with a feeding schedule consisting of 1200kg of assorted bony fish and crustaceans.

Not really sure the part about 'monthly cleaning and upkeep' is necessary, and 'to coincide with a feeding schedule' feels awkward here.

Due to SCP-X’s anomalous abilities all maintenance, feedings, and interviews are to be conducted solely by female staff.

add a comma after abilities

SCP-X is the collective designation assigned to large anomalous instances of Lophiiformes, or the deep sea anglerfish.

'large' feels vague here; there's an implication this might be meant to be e.g. 'large number of…' as opposed to 'large sized' but? Really my concern is just that 'large' and 'anomalous' doesn't actually tell us anything about the SCP.

In addition, all instances possess an exceptionally long illicium or fishing rod, capable of extending at least 100m.

'fishing rod' doesn't quite clarify what an illicium is enough: I'd suggest cutting that and adding a footnote instead explaining illicium in more words.

In place of the esca or lure, the illicium terminates into a realistic and anatomically accurate body of a human female, connected at the base of the skull.

Same here; or alternatively using "In place of the esca, or lore, the…"

'terminates in a realistic' might be clearer but?

reports of an enormous beached fish near the boardwalks of ███████, ██████ reached imbedded agents within the local police department.

Why is this redacted? In universe, it seems like the location would be important context for researchers, and out of universe, it's an irrelevant detail that is made to seem important via the use of redaction.

and it currently resides in the marine wing of Site-66.

(SCP-X-1 has been allowed to remove its lure from its tank to speak directly to the interviewer.)

IMO: contextualise this more; briefly explain why it's being interviewed.

Dr. ██████

Give this dude a name. It'll make this section much clearer.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Why weren’t we more careful?: Re: Why weren’t we more careful?
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

Okay so I'm gonna be upfront: a lot of my comments here are going to be representative of this being an unfinished work.

The core problem I have with this at the moment is nothing interesting happens: all the interesting events are elided so completely that they have no impact. For example, consider:

Hey I’ve worked with SCP-████ before back when I was a researcher, that’s a fucking safe class SCP how in fucks name did it breach containment?

This implies interesting things! There's a safe class anomaly that somehow breached containment but…nothing really happens here? There's no hint at what the anomaly is so we can't theorise how it might've breached containment, but there's also no hint at what it breaching containment means like, it could be a harmless AI that rolls around in a roomba, or it could be a button that kills everyone if pressed.

The addendums after the exploration log suffer from this a lot: having Cutting request extra help is you saying 'hey this thing is dangerous' when really you should be showing us it being dangerous.

My biggest concern though is that I've read all of what you have so far and I don't know where the story is going: at the moment, it just feels really aimless, and it seems like this is in part because you don't have an aim here. There's a lot of elements that could go somewhere interesting though and it just feels like it needs to decide whether the focus is 'ancient bronze age civilisation', 'powerful being who can destroy whatever' or 'ancient foundation site moved from the present'. I think either the first or the last could work, but it needs to explore it more, I think? My concern with doing the second is you start getting into big SCP-1730 territory and frankly you want to steer this as far away from that as you can.

On the last: a lot of this treats the site as if it was just…moved recently but there's also a lot of places that treat is as mysterious and unknown and it feels like this really needs to settle on handling it in one of the two ways.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

No barriers are to be placed around SCP-XXXX due to risk of discovery by satellites or civilians.

This seems a little counter-intuitive; like, surely you could add barriers a few km away say and then just be all 'radiation leak' or 'dangerous naturally occurring gas' or w/e and it would be more secure?

The area and surroundings that SCP-XXXX occupies

'area' and 'surroundings' seem basically synonymous here and I'd just use one

An underground facility designated Site-██-█ has been constructed near SCP-XXXX for immediate analysis of artefacts or relevant information retrieved from SCP-XXXX

Why is the site redacted? Surely anyone cleared to know about this is also cleared to know where the site is and indeed likely works there?

Any incursion that on-site security is incapable of responding to is to be immediately reported to Site Director Gerald or if necessary, to Site-██.

This phrasing implies that incursions site security can respond to are not to be immediately reported which is a bad idea; but also this feels like something a reader can assume rather than something necessary to say.

Also, if you redact the site people are to report stuff to, how are people meant to know who to report stuff to?

Aerial view of the ████████ of SCP-XXXX recovered from downed Chaos Insurgency drone, it is unknown how said drone was not affected by SCP-XXXX’s effect

Why is someone allowed to see this picture but not see what it is? Why is a reader being shown this picture if we aren't meant to know what it is?

resembling a technologically advanced foundation facility.

'foundation' should be capitalised here

Footnote 1: The object is highly unpredictable and possesses considerable destructive capabilities. A containment breach may escalate into a K-Class scenario, and the object's recontainment is to be considered a high priority. Often assigned to Euclid and Keter class objects.

This is badly placed; I'd probably put it after the end of 'containment breach' but I'd also refocus it on describing what that means in terms of a containment breach, since opening on 'The object is highly unpredictable' is extremely confusing to a reader because we're not sure what that has to do with containment breaches.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a currently undiscovered SCP

The previous sentence basically states this already.

that possesses the ability to manipulate space and time and appears to have caused the containment breach that led to the creation of SCP-XXXX.

I'd add a semi-colon/comma after 'time' just to separate 'space and time' and 'appears' more

The O5 council has ordered the immediate termination of SCP-XXXX-1 as soon as it is discovered (see Protocol-XXXX).

This feels weird; it feels like it needs a little more setup to establish why but??

SCP-XXXX-2 was an unknown Bronze Age civilisation

This needs something more hinting at why it's related to the core scp before introducing it here: I'd probably lead with like, SCP-XXXX-1 wiped out the civilisation say.

Footnote 2: Possibly an offshoot of the ██████ civilisation but is still under speculation

this is a shit redaction. Anything you put in the blackbox is gonna be far more interesting than an open void.

but was wiped out in a mass genocide by SCP-XXXX-1.

genocide implies mass.

SCP-XXXX-1's motivation to do so is unclear. (see exploration logs).

This is….just a weird sentence to include? It feels like this should be where you hook a reader into finding out more about what's happening but it's just so blandly stated that I don't find myself caring about the mystery. Also the first period is unnecessary and I really don't like 'see exploration logs' style bits in a SCP.

SCP-XXXX is in relatively good condition despite both its age

you have to indicate that SCP-XXXX is old before you say 'despite its age' otherwise a reader is like 'huh what?': it feels like the opening paragraph should set this up rather than like, getting distracted for two paragraphs explaining stuff before bringing it up.

Also what does 'relatively good' mean here? It's needlessly vague phrasing.

SCP-XXXX is surrounded by the ruins of structures created by SCP-XXXX-2. (See analysis of surrounding structures)

janky full stop before parenthesis again

It is unknown how or why SCP-XXXX came to be in the ████ desert as Site-██ is currently located at [REDACTED], it is hypothesised that SCP-XXXX-1 used the rotation of the earth to transport Site-██ due to [REDACTED]

Too much redaction.

No personnel were recovered alive from SCP-XXXX

This is a weird statement because it's pretty unclear as to whether it means 'no-one has ever returned from SCP-XXXX alive' or 'we didn't find anyone alive inside SCP-XXXX' and it's also unclear why we'd expect to find someone alive inside SCP-XXXX like…it's 5000 years old?

One foundation guard by the name of Nathaniel ███████

One weird trick to make a character a lot more relatable easily: don't redact their surname.

Footnote 4: As of writing this article there are no plans on changing the D-class identification system

This doesn't quite land for me because there's not been anything establishing what the D-Class identification system in use is so it being different doesn't necessarily land

Discovery

I don't mean to bang this drum again, but every single redaction in this section is a bad redaction with the exception of only "SCP-████". This includes the two [DATA EXPUNGED]'s too.

3 days after the acquisition of SCP-XXXX

'acquisition' feels like a weird way to say this since it's a facility and you can't quite, acquire it?

loud and clear, Confirm all members

random capital

and can't really confirm exactly how far below the Site stretches, it's very possible this is another reality shifting anomaly

the 'really' feels clunky here, as does leaving 'ground' implied rather than explicit. alternatively 'down' would work better than 'below'.

Also it feels like this comma should be a . or at least a ;

evac outta there understood?

comma before understood

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Screams: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

Additionally: please don't reply to yourself like this in future; if you wish to add additional detail to the main post, use the 'Edit' button (under the blue 'Options' in the bottom right corner of the post) to edit the post.
